title.narrative: Social and Economic Reintegration of the survivor Bangladeshi Returnee Migrant Workers (SERe)

description.narrative:
During 2023, 1.3 million Bangladeshis migrated overseas to seek employment (over 9% were women) - a rise of 11% compared to 2022. The main destinations were Saudi Arabia and Malaysia followed by Gulf States. The remittances sent by Bangladeshi migrant workers totalled nearly USD 22 billion in 2023 which plays a significant role to increase the country's foreign currency reserve, having a trickle down effect on the overall economy of the country. Unfortunately, the government does not ensure a fair and ethical recruitment system which puts thousands of workers in a trafficked situation in the migration cycle. Though the government maintains a database of the outgoing migrants, there is no system in place to record the information of the returnees. OKUP has provided direct assistance to the vulnerable returnees since 2010. Roughly 300 to 400 survivor returnees including the victims of trafficking have received direct assistance from OKUP annually.
CAFOD has supported OKUP's work focused on the reintegration of returnee migrant workers since 2016. This project will provide co-funding to OKUP who have managed to secure the majority of the funds needed from the Karuna Trust. It will support survivor returnees, with a special emphasis on women and girl returnee migrants who have been trafficked and abused. Services will include: trauma informed psycho-social support, 'safe homes', medical assistance, legal aid (particularly through arbitration), life skills training to build confidence, and entrepreneurship development training together with follow up mentoring support. OKUP will also build the capacity of Upazila level Migrant Forums to implement an awareness-raising campaign to challenge and change discriminatory attitudes within communities towards returnees - particularly women returnees.
